docs: Catalogue of VS Code extensions that carry a usable language server.
DATA, not code: supporting another extension means adding an entry here.
A .vsix is a zip. An extension implementing a language feature ships the
language server inside it, and that server speaks LSP over stdio like any
other one: it needs no VS Code API and no extension host. So installing it
is a download plus an entry in lsp_servers.json, and the LSP layer itself
is untouched.
Only entries whose handshake was actually verified belong here. An
extension that merely contains a file named *server.js is not enough:
several bundle a server that never answers 'initialize' outside VS Code,
or that needs a module (typically 'typescript') the editor normally
supplies. Those are left out on purpose - see docs/ for the survey.
Extensions that only draw UI (themes, GitLens, Vim, Prettier) carry no
server at all and can never be supported this way.
Per entry:
marketplace       Open VSX '<namespace>/<name>' identifier
display_name      what to show a human
runtime           'node' (run through node) or 'native' (executable)
platform_specific the server is a compiled program, so the download must
ask for this machine's build; the default universal
archive carries no binary at all
entrypoint        path of the server inside the extracted vsix, spelled
the way the Unix build does ('.exe' is tried too)
verified_version  the version this entry was actually handshaked against
notes             caveats worth surfacing at install time
lsp               the servers.json entry, minus 'binary' and the server
path, which the installer fills in once it knows where
the extension landed on disk
